How to update this tool
Updating the tool
1. Get new file from Claude
2. Open it in browser → Command+S to save
3. Make sure filename is exactly portfolio-tracker.html
4. Go to github.com/Tracker1122/Portfolio-Tracker
5. Click + → Upload files → drag file in
6. Click green Commit changes
7. Wait 60 seconds
8. Refresh tracker1122.github.io/Portfolio-Tracker/portfolio-tracker.html
Your data stays — no export/import needed for updates
1Enter ticker, buy date, shares, price paid, and current price
2Enter S&P at buy date — use the historical link top right if needed

ⓘTwo pp methods, two different questions
Industry-level pp (shown on Spotlight cards and Industry Reference headers) is capital-weighted across positions — total $ deficit ÷ total invested. It answers: "how much pp alpha did the capital deployed in this whole industry produce?"
Per-position pp (shown in drill-downs and Strategy Reference rows) is just the position's actual deviation from its theme benchmark. It answers: "how is this single ticker performing vs its theme?"
Strategy Reference
ⓘPer-position pp — pp values shown in this panel are position-specific (this ticker's return minus its theme benchmark over the holding period). They are not capital-weighted across the industry. For industry-aggregate capital-weighted pp, see Industry Reference below or click any Industry Spotlight card.
Industry Reference
ⓘTwo pp methods used in this panel. The pp shown in each industry card header (next to the dollar deficit) is capital-weighted across positions. The per-position pp shown in the drill-down (when you click a card) is position-specific.

True Exposure — Full Breakdown
Index look-through tables (advanced)
Paste your funds’ holdings here to decompose them into stocks above. When you hold a broad index fund (VOO, VTI, QQQ…) or an ETF, you already own its names inside it. Pasting the holdings dissolves that fund into single tickers in the distribution and feeds the hidden-exposure flags on the New Position Evaluation tab. Weights are approximate — refresh them when they drift (e.g. from the fund’s Schwab holdings page). Look-through only fires for funds you actually hold.

Industry Intelligence
Book Performance — Isolate & Compare
Turn off part of the book to see how the rest performs without it. Non-destructive — it filters this view only, never your data. Only directly-held positions can be excluded; a name held only inside an ETF can't be cleanly removed from that ETF's return.
Nothing Burgers
Open lots that have barely moved (within the ± band) — idle capital you can trim with minimal tax drag to fund higher-conviction moves. Sorted by market value, most idle first. PE-locked lots are excluded (can’t be sold).
Add Candidates
Positions beating both SPX and theme by ≥+$300. Tier 1 = past sleeve soak, fair to consider for adding. Tier 2 = early strength, still in soak — informational only, not action-eligible. Portfolio Balance Plays excluded.

Do I Own It? — Ticker Look-Up
Search any ticker to see whether it’s in your book — held directly, embedded inside your funds (look-through), or both. Useful when you’re not sure you already own something.
ETF & Stock Dissection — holdings overlap
Compare what's inside two ETFs — or an ETF vs a single stock — to see how much they actually overlap. For an ETF, open its full holdings on stockanalysis.com and paste the table (only ticker + % is read — row #, name and shares are ignored). For a stock, just enter its ticker. Overlap is computed on the names you paste and labeled with how much of each fund that covers, so a partial paste is never mistaken for the whole ETF.

Analyze any ticker
Type one or more tickers (space or comma separated) for the same read-out Discovery gives the names hiding in your funds — recent performance, the 📊 price-history deep-dive, ℹ company info, and where it lands in your themes. One Polygon price call per new ticker, then cached.
Decision Scorecard
Risk Review
Checklist — evaluate a single candidate
A structured pre-purchase checklist — it gives you the questions a disciplined buyer asks and organizes your answers, so every candidate runs the same gauntlet your existing positions are judged against. Field hints tell you where on Schwab to find each number and what a good/bad value looks like. After saving, each candidate gets checkable observations (computed facts, no recommendation) and an optional AI for/against/gaps analysis that argues both sides and never concludes — you weigh it. For ETFs it can fetch real holdings and flag overlap with names you hold directly. It does not score or recommend.
